text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts for customer 'HarvestRetail' on dedicated cluster us-west2-dedicated-4. 5m error rate spiked to 11.8% (baseline 0.3%). P95 latency 4.8s. Triggered paging to #incidents.

ryan_oncall: ack - I'm taking this. marking SEV3 for now, will escalate if customer impact persists. @sasha_eng you around?

sasha_eng: around, pulling mem/gpu metrics and kv eviction logs. first glance: node gw-3 showing lots of 502s and `kv_cache_evictions` high.

priya_sre: I'm on pager too. adding tracing link: https://observability.redwood.company/trace?svc=gateway&cluster=us-west2-dedicated-4&from=now-15m

emily_support: HarvestRetail ops (on this thread): we're seeing failures in our order processing endpoints starting ~09:40 PDT. Errors are 502/504. Some customers are retrying and creating duplicates. Please advise ETA.

harvest_retail_ops: additional: spike coincides with a batch job sending a high conc of streaming requests. We're investigating but need a mitigation asap.

ryan_oncall: quick triage checklist: 1) isolate noisy tenant signals 2) apply per-tenant throttles or soft-eviction 3) consider routing a % to hosted fallback or other region 4) monitor error rate.

sasha_eng: running `kubectl top pods -n dedicated-usw2 | grep gw-3` — GPU mem ~95%, CPU ~85%, pod restarts 0. KV cache hit-rate dropped to 22%. Uploading snippet:``` 
[2026-03-15T16:40:02Z] gw-3 kernel: KV cache eviction triggered: active_entries=124562 evicted=78512
[2026-03-15T16:41:10Z] gateway: downstream 502 returned to client harvest-retail /v1/generate
```

priya_sre: looks like noisy neighbor causing KV thrash + GPU pressure leading to 502s when inference path fails fast. Policy: if tenant causes >60% of cache evictions in 5m, apply mitigation. HarvestRetail is at ~67%.

ryan_oncall: emily_support can you confirm if HarvestRetail is on a reserved pool (they are) and whether we have spare capacity to shift them?

emily_support: yes they're on reserved pool us-west2-dedicated-4 (commit). We don't have immediate extra reserved GPUs for them, but we can route a portion of traffic to hosted API temporarily if they accept.

harvest_retail_ops: we can accept partial routing to hosted for non-sensitive endpoints to reduce pressure, yes. Order placing must remain on-dedicated but maybe non-critical analytics can go to hosted.

sasha_eng: plan suggestion: 1) enable per-tenant soft throttle (request token bucket) at the edge for HarvestRetail to 60% of current RPS 2) disable batching for their requests for next 10m (reduces KV pressure) 3) enable fallback for non-critical routes to hosted: route 30% to hosted-us-west and 10% to us-east1-dedicated fallback, if compatible model exists.

ryan_oncall: agree. priya, can you apply throttles & disable batching? I'll coordinate routing change with infra.

priya_sre: applying throttle now: `infractl tenant throttle set --tenant harvest-retail --rps 0.6x --duration 10m`

ops-bot: Command accepted. Throttle applied on edge-tier-2 for tenant harvest-retail.

priya_sre: disabling batching for tenant: `svc-cfg update gateway --tenant harvest-retail --batching=false --ttl 10m`

ops-bot: Config update queued -> deployed to gateways in us-west2 (3/3 nodes).

sasha_eng: monitoring KV metrics... evictions falling already. GPU mem pressure down to 82% on gw-3. 5xx rate dropping to 4.2%.

harvest_retail_ops: seeing immediate drop in 502s on analytics endpoints. Order endpoint still seeing occasional 504s though.

jules_pm: reopening incident to SEV2 given partial customer-impact (order endpoints). need timeline for full restore and customer comms.

ryan_oncall: copying support: emily_support, please send templated update: "We're actively mitigating an issue impacting order endpoints for HarvestRetail. We've applied short-term throttles and routing changes; errors have reduced but we're still investigating a residual timeout. We'll update in 30 minutes or earlier."

emily_support: sending update to customer now.

harvest_retail_ops: thanks. current question: is there a risk of data loss or duplication?

sasha_eng: risk minimal — retries cause duplicates at app layer. We're not dropping requests at storage. Recommend HarvestRetail enable idempotency keys until full fix.

priya_sre: next step: identify offending tenant workload within HarvestRetail (their internal batch job) and advise load shaping. Also start eviction policy for long-lived streams > 60s: `gateway.enforce_max_stream_duration=60s` (per-tenant override).

ryan_oncall: sasha, can you check model variants? maybe switch order endpoint to a smaller quantized variant (faster, less mem) as fallback.

sasha_eng: order endpoint uses model `hf/redwood-retail-v2`. Compatible smaller variant `redwood-retail-v2-q4` exists. Risk: slight quality drop. Recommend route 50% of order traffic to q4 for 15m while we stabilize.

priya_sre: I'm OK to apply that if customer consents. emily_support please confirm with HarvestRetail.

emily_support: asking now — HarvestRetail says: "Quality drop acceptable for retries but core order matching must remain accurate." They consent to 30% routing to q4 for 15m, no more.

ryan_oncall: apply 30% to q4 and keep throttles + batching disabled. Doing routing change: `routingctl modify --tenant harvest-retail --route-order 30%:redwood-retail-v2-q4,70%:redwood-retail-v2 --duration 15m`

ops-bot: Routing change accepted and applied across us-west2 edge proxies.

sasha_eng: post-change metrics: order endpoint 5xx down to 1.6%, mean latency 320ms, p95 1.2s. KV eviction rate stable at baseline.

harvest_retail_ops: order success rate improving — thanks. We'll keep idempotency keys on our side.

jules_pm: great. please capture action items for postmortem: root cause, why throttles weren't auto-triggered earlier, and consider automated tenant-level fallback to quantized model when eviction > threshold.

priya_sre: creating incident ticket IT-2026-894 in the tracker with mitigation steps and timeline.

ryan_oncall: summary for handoff to next oncall (Priya hands to night): current state — throttles active until 10m left, batching disabled for 5m left, routing to q4 at 30% for 10m left. Error rate ~1.4% and trending down. No further action unless >2% or order errors resume.

priya_sre: noted. I'll monitor for next 40 minutes then escalate if it regresses. Handoff checklist posted to incident ticket.

emily_support: final customer update sent: "We applied temporary safeguards; most traffic restored. We're monitoring; next update in 30 minutes or sooner."

harvest_retail_ops: appreciate the fast coordination + temporary routing. We will schedule a change to their batch job.

ryan_oncall: closing active paging. Will convert thread to postmortem doc once Priya files the timeline. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: IncidentBot: paging cleared by ryan_oncall. Incident status: mitigated (customer-functional but partial safeguards). Postmortem requested.

priya_sre: postmortem draft created: https://incidents.redwood.company/IT-2026-894/postmortem — assigning to sasha for root cause analysis.

sasha_eng: will take RCA. initial cause: HarvestRetail internal batch spike causing hot-key KV thrash + GPU mem pressure -> gateway errors; contributing factors: lack of automated tenant fallback to quantized model, insufficient early detection of eviction-driven pressure. Long-term actions: auto-fallback, tenant-level capacity reservation check + alarms, better per-tenant telemetry.

emily_support: marking customer impact closed but recommend follow-up call with HarvestRetail to coordinate changes.

harvest_retail_ops: agree to scheduled call. Thanks everyone.

ryan_oncall: thread closed at 16:58 PDT. Good job team!
